content_html:
Meaning is Relational

Meaning is a pattern of relations. Each spoke (word, photograph, memory, self) gains significance through systems of difference, context, culture, attention, and interaction — not from an intrinsic essence inside the thing.

“Meaning is relational” = meanings are co‑produced by networks of relations. They are neither purely subjective nor purely objective, but emergent from context, use, and interdependence.

Domain Relational Mechanism Example
Language Sign systems; contrast with other signs bank
means money or river by sentence context
Memory Associations; mood/state‑dependent recall Same photo feels different across life stages
Photography Index + framing + viewer + context Caption flips interpretation of an image
Buddhism Dependent origination; emptiness Self arises via causes/conditions, not essence
